description: Graphic on a dark blue background with a bright blue border, centered on a red-white-and-blue campaign-style button reading 'YOUR VOTE COUNTS'. Below it, white text quotes Q-drop language urging viewers to vote and 'fight', signed 'Q'. Get-out-the-vote style image circulated ahead of the 2018 U.S. midterm elections.
text: YOUR VOTE COUNTS. We will do our job to protect the vote. Will you do yours? FIGHT! FIGHT! FIGHT! Q

description: Image of a dark navy yard-sign-style graphic with a corrugated texture. White script text 'Save America!' above a centered U.S. flag, with 'Vote REPUBLICAN' beneath. Partisan get-out-the-vote graphic; filename 'SAVR.jpg' abbreviates the slogan.

FEMA infographic explaining the Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA) system, paired with a photo of a hand holding an iPhone displaying a 'Presidential Alert' test notification. It lists the alert types (Presidential, AMBER, extreme weather), notes users cannot opt out of Presidential Alerts, and states the national WEA test was postponed to October 3, 2018. FEMA logo at bottom left; filename 'POTUS_ALERT.jpg'.
text: Wireless Emergency Alert. The Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA) system sends a message through your mobile carrier. A message box will appear on your phone with a loud tone and vibration. This is different from a text message. Your phone number is not shared with anyone. Can I opt out? By law, you can opt out of general Wireless Emergency Alerts, but not Presidential Alerts. WHAT KIND OF MESSAGES WILL I GET? Presidential Alerts. Meant for use in a national emergency, and the only type of WEA alert that can be sent nationwide by FEMA. AMBER Alerts. Extreme weather and other threatening emergencies. The national WEA test has been postponed to the backup date of October 3, 2018 at 2:18 p.m. EDT. FEMA. FEMAIPAWS. 1:56 PM. Friday 15. Presidential Alert. THIS IS A TEST of the National Wireless Emergency Alert System. No action is needed. Dismiss
